title: Working at Redwood: Careers, Benefits, Hiring & Internal Tools (2026 Update)
author: Marcus Li
body:
Purpose

This consolidated handbook page provides a single-page reference for how we work at Redwood: role families and career ladders, promotion guidance, benefits and perks, the standard hiring workflow, new-hire onboarding expectations (first 90 days), and the set of internal tools engineers and cross-functional partners use daily. People Ops maintains this page; teams should reference specialized pages for role-specific rubrics, compensation bands, or security-sensitive runbooks.

1) High-level culture and working norms

- Mission-aligned: prioritize customer-facing reliability and predictable inference economics.
- Engineering-first, product-minded: ship measurable improvements with tests, monitoring, and docs.
- Trust and autonomy: managers set outcomes; teams decide implementation and tradeoffs.
- Async by default: prefer documented decisions and brief synchronous meetings for alignment.

Working hours and remote policy:
- Hybrid-friendly: employees may work remote or from the office; teams set expected overlap windows (recommended 10:00-16:00 local) for collaboration.
- Travel: company-sponsored travel requires manager approval and expense submission within 10 business days.

Communication expectations:
- Proposals: all cross-team technical proposals should link to a Confluence doc and include success metrics and rollback plan.
- Meeting etiquette: agenda required for meetings >30 minutes; takeaways posted to Confluence as action items.

2) Roles, leveling and career ladders (summary)

Role families supported at Redwood: Engineering (Serving Runtime, Infra, Platform, SRE), Product, Research / Applied ML, Developer Experience, People Ops, Sales / GTM, Customer Success, Finance & Legal.

Leveling principles:
- Outcome-driven: promotion decisions favor demonstrated impact across team or company metrics, documentation of tradeoffs, and mentoring.
- Competency areas: technical craft, execution & ownership, leadership & influence, and cross-functional impact.

Example ladder snapshot (brief):
- IC1 (Associate): executes with mentorship; focuses on learning and reliable delivery.
- IC2 (Mid): owns components; delivers end-to-end features; begins mentoring.
- IC3 (Senior / Staff): leads designs across projects; raises quality and reliability; coaches others.
- IC4 (Principal): shapes technical strategy across teams; accountable for large-scale outcomes and strategy.

Promotion process (practical steps):
1. Employee prepares a promotion packet: one-page impact summary, 3-6 supporting artifacts (PRs, design docs, runbook links), and manager note.
2. Manager submits packet to People Ops and recommends reviewers.
3. Calibration and review: cross-functional interviewers (if applicable) and a calibration panel review evidence against the rubric.
4. Outcome and next-steps: People Ops communicates results; if promoted, compensation/grade updated and role profile published.

Manager checklist for development:
- Maintain 1:1 notes and a written 30/60/90 plan.
- Provide quarterly written feedback.
- Sponsor stretch projects and ensure visibility for high-impact work.

3) Benefits & perks (concise)

Medical & financial:
- Medical, dental, vision: multiple plan tiers; Redwood pays majority of employee premium.
- 401(k) with company match per plan year; vesting schedule on equity grants noted in offer.

Time off & family policies:
- PTO: flexible policy; recommended minimum of 15 days/year.
- Holidays: 12 observed company holidays plus a winter office closure (Dec 25-Jan 1).
- Parental leave: inclusive policy for primary and secondary caregivers; phased return options and manager-supported ramp plans.

Learning & wellness:
- L&D stipend: $1,500 USD annual; manager approval required for conferences over $500.
- Wellness allowance: annual stipend for mental/physical health services.
- Home office: one-time setup stipend at hire and refresh requests evaluated annually.

How to use benefits:
- Enrollment and plan details live in the Benefits portal (linked from People Ops homepage). Open benefits questions to benefits@redwood.com.

4) Hiring process (standard workflow)

Overview steps:
1. Requisition: Hiring manager opens a req in Greenhouse and attaches the hiring doc and scorecard.
2. Sourcing & screen: Recruiting sources; recruiter screens for role fit.
3. Interview loop: role-specific loop with technical assessment and cross-functional interviews.
4. Calibration & decision: interviewers submit scorecards; hiring manager synthesizes feedback.
5. Offer: recruiter extends offer and coordinates comp approvals.
6. Background checks: completed pre-start.

Interviewer guide (key rules):
- Use the standardized role rubric and Greenhouse scorecards.
- Provide feedback within 48 hours; emphasize evidence-based observations.
- Avoid closed interview questions about protected characteristics.

Inclusive hiring practices:
- Diverse slate requirement: aim to include diverse candidates for all open roles where feasible.
- Interviewer training: mandatory unconscious bias and inclusive interviewing curriculum for all interviewers.

5) New-hire onboarding (first 90 days)

Pre-start (Day -7 to 0):
- Offer acceptance: People Ops triggers IT provisioning (Okta, 1Password, email alias), equipment order, and first-week calendar.

Day 0-1: Welcome and access
- IT checklist: verify SSO, 2FA, 1Password vault access, and Google Workspace account.
- Orientation sessions: People Ops overview, security training, and benefits enrollment walkthrough.

Week 1: Team ramp and small tasks
- Manager 1:1 to set 30/60/90 goals.
- Environment setup: local dev environment, repo access, and runbook reading.
- Buddy assignment: each new hire receives a cross-team buddy for practical questions.

Weeks 2-4: Deeper integration
- Ship a small-first-PR: expect a small, reviewer-approved contribution within first 30 days.
- Stakeholder introductions: scheduled meetings with cross-functional partners and product owners.

Month 2-3: Ownership and feedback
- First project ownership: lead a small feature or reliability task.
- 30/90 check-ins: onboarding retros with People Ops and manager; adjustments to ramp plan.

Onboarding checklist (short):
- HR paperwork completed and benefits enrolled.
- Okta and 2FA enabled; 1Password setup completed.
- Joined Slack, relevant Google groups, and Confluence spaces.
- GitHub access granted and local build verified.
- Security and data handling training done within 7 days.

6) Internal tools quick reference (owners & tips)

Primary tools and common tasks:
- Slack (People Ops admin): channels for team communication; use threads, and set Do Not Disturb for focus time.
- Confluence (People Ops owner): store canonical docs, runbooks, and onboarding materials. Use templates for design proposals and postmortems.
- GitHub (Eng Platform owner): code hosting and PRs; follow repo CONTRIBUTING.md and branch protection rules.
- Okta + 1Password (Security owner): SSO and secret management; rotate shared secrets per security policy.
- Greenhouse (Talent Acquisition): interview scheduling and scorecards; interviewers must submit feedback within 48 hours.
- PagerDuty (SRE owner): paging and oncall alerts; follow runbooks for incident response.

Access process and escalation:
1. Baseline access: People Ops provisions base tools via Okta on Day 0.
2. Additional access: manager files an Access Request (Confluence -> templates -> Access Request) with required justification.
3. Emergency escalation: email infra-admins@redwood.com and create a ticket in the IT tracker.

Developer quickstarts (links & commands):
- Repo bootstrap: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/platform.git && make setup-local
- Run a service locally: ./scripts/run-local --service inference-api
- CI/CD: follow eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build runbook and use the PR template for all changes.

7) Career development and ongoing support

Reviews and feedback cadence:
- Performance reviews: formal review cycles are semi-annual; calibration meetings run by People Ops.
- Continuous feedback: encourage written notes in 1:1s and use peer feedback forms for promotion packets.

Mentorship and growth programs:
- Mentorship: engineering mentorship pairs are matched quarterly; managers recommend pairings.
- Learning: internal tech talks, recorded sessions, and L&D reimbursements tracked via People Ops.

8) Contacts and where to get help

- People Ops (general): people-ops@redwood.com
- Benefits & Payroll: benefits@redwood.com
- IT Helpdesk & Access: it-helpdesk@redwood.com
- Recruiting: talent@redwood.com
- Security (Okta/SSO): security@redwood.com
- Oncall & Incidents: oncall@redwood.com (PagerDuty)

FAQ (short)
- Q: How do I request additional GitHub access?
  A: Ask your manager to submit the Access Request template with repo names and justification; infra will process within 3 business days.
- Q: Where are promotion rubrics stored?
  A: Confluence -> People Ops -> Career ladders. Managers also share role-specific rubrics during onboarding.

Document ownership and updates
- Owner: People Ops. Submit edits via page comments or propose major changes through the handbook PR process.
- Change log: 2025-09-15 created; 2026-03-01 updated to reflect onboarding and Okta provisioning improvements.
